title: Heaps and Priority Queues
summary: The binary heap - a complete tree stored in an array, sift-up and sift-down, push and pop in O(log n), building a heap in O(n), heapsort, std::priority_queue and the heap algorithms, min-heaps with std::greater, and classic uses - top k, merging k sorted lists, and the running median with two heaps.

cards.q: In an array-stored heap, where are the children of the node at index 5?
Why is building a heap bottom-up O(n) rather than O(n log n)?
cards.a:
Most nodes are near the bottom, where sifts are short

Half the nodes are leaves, a quarter move at most one level, and so on, so the total work sums to less than n.

cards.q: How do you find the 10 largest values in a stream of a billion numbers?
cards.a:
Keep a min-heap of the 10 largest so far

Whenever the heap holds 11, pop its top: the smallest of the current top values, the one to throw out.
